title: Thrice Happy Souls, Who, Born from Heaven
description: Thrice Happy Souls, Who, Born from Heaven in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 342 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Walking with God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thrice hap-py souls, who, born from heaven, While yet they so-journ here, Do all their days with God be-gin, And spend them in his fear.

lines: Thrice happy souls, who, born from heaven,
Do all their days with God begin,
And spend them in his fear.
And while the world our hands employs,
We'll seek the shelter of thy wings,
In solid, pure delights like these,
Let all our days be past;
Nor shall we then impatient wish,
Nor shall we fear, the last.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
